cards.title: Your A1 checkpoint
sections: Try the five tasks before opening the models. A partner may speak slowly or repeat. Listen to the dictation and write what you hear.
Introduce your role and describe one routine.
Ask about a free time and make a simple invitation.
Say one thing you can do and one thing you cannot do.
Say what a person is doing now.

Write a short reply accepting or declining an invitation.
Review words: foot, leg, arm, tired, grill. Cover the list; recall meanings and use two in your own sentences.
cards.name: Everyday English - A1 - Day 150 - Review & Check - 01
cards.answer:
Dictation: Puck's foot hurts.
1: For example: I’m a student. I study after dinner.
2: For example: Are you free on Saturday? Can you come for lunch?
3: For example: I can swim. I can’t run far.
4: For example: She is writing a message now.
5: For example: Thank you. Yes, I can come at six. Or: Sorry, I’m busy then.
For each task, note: I can do it; I can do it with repetition; I need more practice. Repeat difficult tasks another day with new details. Clear meaning matters more than a perfect accent.
